title: POC Weekly Sync - Quantization INT8/FP8
summary: Weekly POC sync to review quantization experiments. Team reviewed INT8 and FP8 runs vs baseline FP16, discussed small quality regressions on edge cases, confirmed 1.8-2.3x token throughput improvement on INT8, FP8 showing intermediate perf with slightly better quality than INT8. Agreed on action items: run larger 500-prompt eval with production prompts, test INT8 with larger batch sizes and KV-cache warmup, and share updated benchmark spreadsheet and cost delta estimates.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-05-20 14:00 PDT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Alice Nguyen (Redwood AE), Ben Ortiz (Redwood SE), Tom Becker (Acme ML Lead), Maria Lopez (Acme Eng), Samir Patel (Acme SRE), Jin Park (Acme Product)

[00:00] Alice (Redwood AE): Okay, hi everyone, thanks for joining. Quick agenda — status on the quant runs, go over the quality slides Ben put together, and plan next steps. Tom you mentioned you had a few edge cases to call out?
[00:18] Tom (Acme ML Lead): Yep, thanks Alice. We ran your INT8 build yesterday on a subset and saw pretty promising throughput, we also noticed a couple of hallucination-ish outputs on long-context prompts, that's what I wanted to flag early.
[00:30] Ben (Redwood SE): Right, good callout. The short version: INT8 gives roughly 1.8x to 2.3x throughput depending on sequence length and batching. FP8 sits between INT8 and FP16 on perf — closer to INT8 for short sequences but wider gap for long sequences. Quality-wise, INT8 had small regressions on rare syntactic prompts, FP8 had smaller regressions but slightly higher memory than INT8.
[00:56] Maria (Acme Eng): When you say regressions, is that BLEU or F1, or are these human-reviewed examples?
[01:05] Ben: Good question. We ran a mixed eval: automatic metrics (ROUGE-L, exact-match for QA slices) and a small human spot-check set for 100 edge prompts. Automatic metrics show a 0.8–1.5% drop on ROUGE for INT8 vs FP16 on the full eval. For the human spot-check, INT8 had 6/100 borderline answers vs 2/100 for FP16; FP8 had 3/100. So it's small but noticeable on edge cases.
[01:35] Tom: That aligns with what we saw — acceptable overall but some high-value flows are sensitive. Our success criteria calls out <2% quality delta on the production prompt set.
[01:44] Alice: Right, so the threshold is tight. Ben, did you try different per-layer quantization configs or any mixed precision?
[01:52] Ben: Yes — we ran symmetric INT8 across most layers but kept attention kernel in FP16 for stability in one config; that recovered a chunk of the quality. There's a config where we keep the final LM head in FP16 and quantize the rest to INT8 — quality improved back to about 0.4% delta while still getting ~1.6x throughput. We'll share the exact config in the spreadsheet.
[02:20] Samir (SRE): Curious on memory — what savings on peak GPU memory? We're budgeting for Dedicated capacity and need to estimate instance sizing.
[02:29] Ben: On our test model, INT8 reduced peak GPU memory by ~38% vs FP16 which lets you fit about 1.6x larger batch or reduce to a smaller GPU class. FP8 was around 25% reduction. So cost-wise INT8 is the biggest win.
[02:45] Jin (Product): Do those numbers factor KV-cache growth for long chat contexts? We have some customers keeping 8k+ context tokens.
[02:54] Ben: Good point — the numbers above are for 2k context typical. With larger KV caches the effective memory savings shrink because KV cache is often stored in FP16 in our current runtime for numerical stability, but we're experimenting with quantizing KV cache to INT8 for storage (with dequantization on use). Early tests show additional savings but potential latency hit on first token.
[03:22] Tom: So is it safe to say KV cache stays FP16 for now in our recommended config?
[03:27] Alice: For the POC, yes — recommend we keep KV cache FP16 and quantize weights. Ben will test INT8 KV cache as a follow-up.
[03:36] Maria: Can you share the spreadsheet link? The one you shared last week was helpful but hard to follow the configs.
[03:42] Alice: Sure, I'll resend an updated sheet. Ben, did you add a tab with normalized per-token cost?
[03:47] Ben: Yep — there's a cost model tab with per-token cost projections for Hosted and Dedicated, assuming current AWS GPU pricing; we normalized to per-1k tokens. For INT8 we project 30–45% cost reduction vs FP16 depending on batching. There's a link to the raw logs and the benchmark spreadsheet in the notes.
[04:06] Tom: We'll need those numbers tied to our committed throughput for Dedicated — Samir can help with that.
[04:11] Samir: Yep, will correlate. Also need to test VPC peering and our internal tooling. I started setting up a test VPC and will share creds once Alice's team confirms the private deploy checklist.
[04:25] Ben: One other nuance — latency P50/P95 look great for INT8 at small batches, but P99 can spike if the runtime falls back or does CPU-side dequant for some ops. We're working on smoothing that with kernel selection.
[04:42] Maria: Any idea of the P99 numbers?
[04:45] Ben: For 512-token sequences, P99 for FP16 was ~420ms, INT8 P99 was ~560ms in our runs (so higher), FP8 P99 ~500ms. But P50/P95 were lower for INT8. The spikes often correlate with attention kernel fallback on certain sequence lengths.
[05:05] Tom: That's concerning for user-facing latency SLAs. Is there an autodisable flag to force FP16 for latency-critical endpoints?
[05:11] Alice: Yes — in Redwood config you can pin a model variant to FP16 for a route or tag it as latency-critical. Also can use smart routing to send to faster but more expensive capacity.
[05:20] Jin: For the POC, let's test three routes: INT8 for bulk inference, FP8 for mixed workloads, and FP16 for a small latency-critical fleet.
[05:30] Ben: Sounds good. We'll prepare sample route configs and suggested autoscale settings.
[05:36] Maria: About quality checks — can you run a confusion analysis or token-level diffs for the edge cases? We want to understand pattern of failure (hallucination, truncation, formatting).
[05:48] Ben: Yes — we have a diff tool and a small human-in-the-loop review. Plan to include a CSV with flagged diffs per prompt. That will be part of the 500-prompt run.
[06:00] Tom: Timeline recap — we want a full 500-prompt run by next week and the VPC checklist by Tuesday. If quality is within 2% we can sign off to move to a pilot.
[06:12] Alice: Agreed. Any blockers?
[06:15] Samir: Slight blocker — need the test VPC IPs and exact network rules from Redwood to finish peering.
[06:22] Alice: We'll send the private deployment checklist and sample security group rules after this call.
[06:28] Ben: Also note that the INT8 quantization pipeline we used is an internal toolchain that we can package for Dedicated/private deployments, but we recommend testing on a small sample first. There's a potential for model-specific tuning.
[06:41] Jin: Are there any licensing or compliance implications with the quant toolchain?
[06:45] Alice: No new licensing — it's part of Redwood platform. For compliance, we'll include notes in the security pack.
[06:52] Tom: One more question — cost estimates: can you give rough monthly savings if we convert 70% of our inference to INT8?
[06:59] Ben: Very rough: if 70% of 10M tokens/month run on INT8 with 35% per-token cost reduction, that's roughly a 24% reduction in total inference spend — I'll put proper numbers in the spreadsheet.
[07:13] Maria: Great. Also we noticed some transcription glitches in earlier sheet names, hope the next link is cleaner.
[07:18] Alice: Apologies — we'll tidy it.
[07:20] Ben: I'll attach raw logs, the normalized cost tab, and the config snippets for mixed-precision.
[07:27] Tom: Thanks. Let's recap actions and owners.
[07:30] Alice: Recap: Ben runs 500 prompts and shares diffs; Alice sends updated sheet and private deploy checklist; Samir finishes VPC setup; Tom delivers final prompt set; Maria trials larger batch sizes. Next sync same time next week unless we need a mid-week checkpoint.
[07:50] Tom: Works for us. Thanks everyone.
[07:55] Alice: Thanks all — meeting adjourned.

Notes/links referenced: Benchmark spreadsheet (redwood/quant-bench-2025-05-19.xlsx), raw-run logs (s3://redwood-logs/poc/acme/2025-05-19/), private deploy checklist (link will be shared).
notes: Ben uploaded the detailed comparison spreadsheet under the shared drive (will resend)
Recommended config: partial FP16 (LM head + attention) + INT8 weights for best quality/perf tradeoff
FP8 shows intermediate perf with slightly better quality than INT8 but less memory savings
